title: Analytics observability contracts for console usage pipelines
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: Define unambiguous SLIs, SLO targets, tracing and log schemas, and dashboard requirements for the Console usage analytics pipelines. This ticket produces the ‘observability contract’ that downstream engineering teams will implement so that ingestion, transformation, and aggregation stages emit consistent metrics and traces.

Scope:
- SLI definitions for ingestion, processing, and freshness across pipeline stages (ingest, enrich, aggregate, export).
- Concrete SLO targets and measurement windows.
- Trace/span naming conventions and required attributes (message IDs, dataset IDs, hashed customer_id, processing attempt, partition offsets).
- Logging schema (structured JSON fields, severity rules, correlation ids) and retention guidance.
- Sampling policy for traces and logs and exception rules for high-priority customers and errors.
- Dashboard and alerting requirements (Grafana + BigQuery + Prometheus mapping).
- Rollout plan and required instrumentation changes for console-backend, analytics-ingester, and transform workers.

Acceptance criteria:
- A single markdown artifact (Confluence page) exists with: SLI formulas, SLOs, trace attribute list, log JSON schema, sampling table, and dashboard wireframes.
- Instrumentation checklist completed for three services: console-backend, analytics-ingester, transform-workers.
- Prometheus metric names and labels documented and exported by each service; example queries for p50/p95/p99 latency and error-rate.
- Traces emitted using OpenTelemetry with consistent service/span naming and mandatory attributes; proof-of-concept traces visible in staging Grafana Tempo.
- Dashboards + alerts created in staging and validated with synthetic traffic.

SLIs & SLO proposals (initial):
- Ingestion success rate: ratio of messages accepted by analytics-ingester to messages produced to Kafka topic over 24h; SLO 99.95% (rolling 30d).
- Processing latency by stage: p50/p95/p99 for end-to-end processing time (ingest -> export); SLO p95 < 350ms for interactive paths, p99 < 2s for batch transforms.
- Freshness: time between event timestamp and availability in aggregation tables; SLO 99% of events <= 5 minutes.
- Transformation error rate: percentage of records dropped due to transform errors; SLO < 0.1% per dataset.
- Backfill catch-up time: measured for incident recovery; target < 6h for < 24h backlog.

Trace & log schema (high level):
- Required trace attributes: trace_id, span_id, parent_span_id, service_name, span_type (ingest|transform|aggregate|export), message_id, dataset_id, customer_id_hashed, partition, kafka_offset, processing_attempt, stage_latency_ms.
- Span naming: {service_name}.{span_type}.{operation} (e.g., analytics-ingester.ingest.write-kv).
- Logs: structured JSON with keys: timestamp, level, message, trace_id, span_id, message_id, dataset_id, customer_tier, error_code, stack, extra (freeform). Must not contain PII (customer_id must be hashed).
- Sampling policy: default 1% for success traces, 100% for errors and severity >= ERROR, 100% for internal customers flagged as P0. Provide route to temporarily increase sampling for incidents.

Observability telemetry export:
- Metrics: expose Prometheus counters/histograms with labels: service, dataset, tenant_hash, stage. Document metric names: analytics_ingest_received_total, analytics_ingest_success_total, analytics_stage_latency_seconds_bucket, analytics_transform_errors_total.
- Traces: instrument with OpenTelemetry SDK (OTLP exporter to Tempo/OTEL collector).
- Logs: structured JSON to Loki/Cloud Logging with index fields mapped for dashboards.

Dashboards & alerts:
- Grafana dashboards: Overview (ingest rate, success rate, latency heatmap), Per-tenant health (top-50 tenants by error rate), Pipeline timeline (lag/backlog), Cost indicators (high-cardinality cardinality spikes).
- Alert rules: PagerDuty for SLO burn rate > 4x over 1h or ingestion success < 99.5% for 5m. Medium alerts to Slack channel #analytics-ops for < 99.8% success for 15m.

Implementation plan:
1) Finalize contract doc and share with teams (3 days).
2) Instrumentation spike: add minimal OTEL + Prom exporter to analytics-ingester and console-backend (1 week).
3) Implement schema changes across transform-workers (2 weeks parallel).
4) Deploy to staging, generate synthetic traffic and validate dashboards/alerts (4 days).
5) Canary rollout to 10% traffic and monitor SLOs for 72h (3 days).
6) Full rollout with postmortem checklist and runbooks (2 days).

Tradeoffs & design decisions:
- Retention vs cost: propose 30d full-resolution traces, 90d aggregated metrics. Higher retention for P0 tenants only.
- Sampling: default low sampling reduces cost but increases debugging friction for transient bugs; mitigation: error-level full sampling and quick-on toggles via feature flags.
- Tag cardinality: avoid including high-cardinality fields (raw customer_id) in metric labels; only include tenant_hash. For ad-hoc investigations use logs/bigquery exports.

Rollout & follow-ups:
- Create linked tasks to update SDK libs in each repo (ENG-8390, ENG-8391).
- Cost review with infra finance before enabling full trace retention (ENG-8420).
- Add SLO dashboard to executive weekly health report template (PM-402).

Links & artifacts:
- Confluence SLO draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/AN/Analytics+Observability+Contracts
- Prototype dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/analytics-observability/staging-overview
- Implementation spike PR (console): https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1234
- OTEL collector config (staging): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-config/pull/88

Risks:
- Under-instrumented services may mask systemic failures; mitigate with mandatory checklist.
- Cost overruns from trace retention; gate with finance approval.

Next steps: finalize the Confluence doc, schedule review with Observability Guild, and create per-repo subtasks for instrumentation and export config updates.
